exercise.name: Dumbbell Step-up

reference.title: Dumbbell Step-up
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

exercise.laterality: Unilateral (lead leg works up and down)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you drive up onto the bench, inhale as you step down.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short stand on top, about 1.5 s down with the lead leg controlling

prescription.tempo: Up in about 1 s, down in 1.5-2 s
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, then slower lowering (3 s). Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set. Simenz 2012 used 6RM loads.

cues.text: Stand tall facing the end of the bench, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides.
Place the whole right foot on the bench, knee over the middle of the foot.
Breathe out and drive through the right heel to stand up; the left foot follows without pushing hard.
Stand tall on the bench, dumbbells hanging still.
Breathe in and step the left foot down behind you slowly; the right leg does the lowering.
Bring the right foot down beside the left.
Reset and repeat on the same leg, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing off the floor with the back foot
mistakes.fix: Keep the back foot light; the lead leg does the work.
Keep the knee over the 2nd-3rd toe.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning far forward and swinging the dumbbells
mistakes.fix: Stay tall; let the dumbbells hang straight down.
Lower under control; the lead leg bends to let the back foot reach the floor.

kinematics.norm: Simenz 2012 used a 45.7 cm box for loaded step-ups; lower steps (15-20 cm) bend the knee less (Smutnick 2009)
About 120 degrees at foot contact on a 40.6 cm step (Smutnick 2009); a little more on 45 cm
About 92 degrees on a 40.6 cm step (Smutnick 2009)
Bends until the back foot reaches the floor (clinical opinion)
Slight forward lean over the lead foot (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up, 1.5-2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Simenz, Garceau, Lutsch, Suchomel & Ebben 2012, electromyographical analysis of lower extremity muscle activation during variations of the loaded step-up exercise (J Strength Cond Res 26(12):3398-3405)
Krause Neto, Soares, Vieira et al. 2020, gluteus maximus activation during common strength and hypertrophy exercises: a systematic review (J Sports Sci Med 19(1):195-203)
Smutnick & Bohannon 2009, hip and knee flexion of lead and trail limbs during ascent of a step of different heights by normal adults (Physiotherapy 95(4))

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a stable bench that cannot slide or tip; step onto the middle of the pad.
modify: Knee pain: use a lower step (15-30 cm).
Balance concerns: one dumbbell, free hand on a rail.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Lead-leg knee extensors drive the body up and control the step down; the lead knee starts deeply bent on a bench this high (about 120 degrees at 40.6 cm in Smutnick 2009).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Lead-leg knee extensors drive the body up and control the step down; the lead knee starts deeply bent on a bench this high (about 120 degrees at 40.6 cm in Smutnick 2009).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Lead-leg hip extensor. Step-up variations were among the exercises with the highest gluteus maximus activation, above 60% MVIC (Krause Neto 2020); Simenz 2012 tested them on a 45.7 cm box with 6RM loads.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Lead-leg hip extensor. Step-up variations were among the exercises with the highest gluteus maximus activation, above 60% MVIC (Krause Neto 2020); Simenz 2012 tested them on a 45.7 cm box with 6RM loads.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension from the deep start position.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension from the deep start position.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and steady the knee (Simenz 2012 measured biceps femoris and semitendinosus).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and steady the knee (Simenz 2012 measured biceps femoris and semitendinosus).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the lead shin on the bench; the trailing calf gives a small push-off.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the lead shin on the bench; the trailing calf gives a small push-off.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (Simenz 2012 measured it in all step-up variations).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (Simenz 2012 measured it in all step-up variations).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall with a dumbbell hanging from each hand.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright as it leans slightly over the lead foot.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright as it leans slightly over the lead foot.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders level and stop the dumbbells pulling the shoulder blades down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders level and stop the dumbbells pulling the shoulder blades down (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Hips rise up and forward over the bench foot
